statement: When the whole number N is divided by 9 the remainder is 4. When the whole number M is divided by 9 the remainder is 7. What is the remainder when N x M is divided by 9?

choices.misconception: I added the remainders and did not reduce the answer.
I multiplied the remainders but forgot to divide 28 by 9.
I added the remainders instead of multiplying them.
I subtracted the smaller remainder from the larger.

hints: Remainders: the remainder of a product depends only on the remainders of the factors. Multiply the remainders, then take the remainder of that result.

solutions.reliable: Write N = 9a + 4 and M = 9b + 7. Every part of the product N x M is a multiple of 9 except 4 x 7 = 28, and 28 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 9. So N x M leaves remainder 1. The transferable idea: multiply remainders, then reduce, because the multiples of the divisor drop out.
solutions.elegant: Test real numbers: N = 13 and M = 16 give 208 = 23 x 9 + 1. Remainder 1 again.

whyOnTest: Remainders of products are the heart of modular reasoning, and the trap is forgetting to reduce the product of the remainders.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
